records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with a single `/`, so protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/img.png`) and relative paths without a leading slash fall through unchanged. Protocol-relative URLs get mangled into `http://<host>//cdn...` broken links in imported posts; feed authors whose sites use protocol-relative assets see broken images/links in every embedded copy of the article.
records.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links/images are rewritten only when `href/src.start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` also satisfy this, and then `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `"#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/img.png"` (where `prefix` is the importing site like `http://eviltrout.com`). That mangles protocol-relative assets into broken URLs. Relative paths without a leading slash are also left unchanged by this logic.

Anyone can curl /embed/best with a spoofed Referer matching embeddable_host and enumerate/render any topic's content via the TopicView branch (topic_id_for_embed performs no referer-independent scoping). The actual SSRF protection of the retriever does not depend on this check, so impact is limited to unauthorized content disclosure/crawling of a forum intended to be restricted to embedding on one host — but the gate provides no real boundary.

The Referer header is attacker-controlled and includes arbitrary path/query data; ERB's HTML escaping of quotes (to ') prevents JS execution but produces a malformed string / syntax error when the referer contains a single quote, breaking the resize postMessage for those embeds. Any string header interpolated into a script context should be JSON-encoded, not HTML-escaped.
records.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the inline script does `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>');`, directly interpolating the attacker-controlled Referer header into a JavaScript string literal. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses Kernel#open on a configuration value, which executes shell commands when the value begins with a pipe character. Ruby's open() treats a string starting with '|' as a command to run, so any actor able to set site settings (or compromise the settings store) gets arbitrary command execution on the app server rather than just an HTTP fetch. Per the config-as-attacker-input threat model, config-backed sinks into open() should be treated as command-injection-capable; use open-uri's URI(...) or Net::HTTP instead.
records.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. Because `open()` with a String argument can invoke `Kernel#open` semantics (and in Ruby a string starting with `|` is treated as a command), a configuration-controlled `feed_polling_url` can become a command-execution sink rather than a pure HTTP fetch. This matches the finding’s command-injection mechanism.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url) with the user-supplied embed_url, and open() invokes command execution for pipe-prefixed strings. The invalid_host? check (URI(@embed_url).host == embeddable_host) rejects pipe-prefixed strings since URI() raises, so this path is currently contained; but the safety depends on TopicRetriever always running before import_remote — the Disqus thor task calls import_remote directly with t[:link] from a local file, so any future caller that skips the retriever check gets command execution from unvalidated input. The command-injection primitive (Kernel#open on untrusted URLs) should be removed, not merely gated upstream.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new topic_embeds migration uses force: true on a table that, once shipped and populated, will be dropped and its data lost if the migration is ever re-run (redo, or a fresh db:migrate against an environment where the table pre-exists from a prior deploy). After this migration ships and TopicEmbed rows accumulate, any db:migrate:redo or rollback+re-run wipes every topic_embed mapping; embedded sites then re-import articles as duplicate topics because embed_url lookups find nothing, silently forking comment threads off existing posts.
records.rationale: The migration explicitly uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb), and `force: true` will drop an existing table before creating it. If `topic_embeds` already exists for any reason (prior branch deploy, manual creation), running this migration can silently destroy existing embed mappings, leading to orphaned/duplicate imports as described.

records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import returns nil silently when PostCreator.create fails, and the RetrieveTopic job then completes 'successfully' with no topic created, so the embed iframe loops on the loading page forever. The embed controller renders 'loading' and reloads every 30s (loading.html.erb); if the article fetch fails or the post is rejected (e.g., empty title/content after readability extraction), the job enqueued from EmbedController#best completes with no error, no embed row is created, and the visitor's browser reloads /embed/best in an infinite loop with no error ever surfaced to the user or the logs.
records.rationale: `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally schedules `document.location.reload()` every 30000ms with no attempt limit or success/failure check. `EmbedController#best` renders this loading view whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, so if topic retrieval never produces an embed (e.g., missing `embed_by_username` causes `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` to `return if user.blank?`, or other retrieval failures), the iframe will reload indefinitely and keep re-triggering the loading state (and job enqueueing/throttled retrieval attempts).

records.issue_text: [BUG] A single bad feed item aborts the whole items loop with an unhandled NoMethodError (i.content or i.title nil for a valid Atom entry), and with sidekiq_options retry: false the remaining items are permanently dropped with no retry. The first item missing content raises NoMethodError on i.content.scrub; every subsequent item in the feed is skipped, and because retry is disabled there is no later attempt — feed items are silently missing from the forum with no log identifying which item broke the run.
records.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` inside `rss.items.each`. If a feed item has no `content` (i.e., `i.content` is `nil`), calling `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, crashing the job before processing subsequent items. The job also sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures won’t be retried automatically.
